subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Explore numbers with simple, everyday examples.

lessons.title: Add in friendly steps
lessons.text: You can break numbers into smaller parts to add them. To find 8 + 5, split 5 into 2 and 3. First make ten: 8 + 2 = 10. Then add 3 to get 13.
lessons.hint: Split 4 into 1 and 3. Add 1 to 9 first.

lessons.title: Make equal groups
lessons.text: Multiplication is a way to count equal groups. If you have 3 bags with 2 apples in each bag, you have 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 apples. We can write this as 3 × 2 = 6.
lessons.q: There are 4 baskets with 3 apples in each. How many apples are there?

lessons.title: Share into fractions
lessons.text: A fraction names equal parts of a whole. If a sandwich is cut into 4 equal pieces, each piece is one fourth. The bottom number tells how many equal pieces make the whole.
lessons.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 1 slice. What fraction did you eat?
lessons.hint: You ate 1 of the 4 equal parts.
lessons.why: One out of four equal parts is one fourth, written 1/4.

subjects.name: Reading & language
subjects.description: Read a little. Discover something new.

lessons.title: Follow the story
lessons.text: Read this short story: “Leo put a seed in a pot. He watered it each day. A week later, a tiny green leaf appeared.” Stories often tell what happens first, next, and last.
options: He put a seed in a pot.
lessons.hint: Go back to the first sentence.
lessons.why: The story begins with Leo putting a seed in a pot.

lessons.title: Use word clues
lessons.text: The words around a new word can help you understand it. Read: “The puppy was tiny. It was small enough to fit in a little basket.” The second sentence gives a clue about tiny.
lessons.q: What does “tiny” mean in this story?
lessons.hint: Think about the size of the puppy’s basket.
lessons.why: Tiny means very small. The little basket is a clue.

lessons.title: Find the main idea
lessons.text: The main idea is what a passage is mostly about. Read: “Bees visit flowers to collect food. As they move, they carry pollen between flowers. This helps many plants make seeds.”
lessons.q: What is this passage mostly about?
lessons.hint: What do all three sentences tell you about?
lessons.why: The sentences describe bees visiting flowers and helping plants make seeds.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.description: Look closely at the world around you.

lessons.title: Use your observations
lessons.text: An observation is something you notice with your senses or a measuring tool. “This leaf is green” is an observation. “This is the best leaf” is an opinion.
options: This rock has three white spots.
lessons.hint: Choose something you could check by looking at the rock.
lessons.why: You can look closely and count three white spots.

lessons.title: What plants need
lessons.text: Most familiar green plants need light, water, air, and nutrients to grow. Their roots take in water. Their leaves use light to help make food.
lessons.q: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
lessons.hint: Think about the part that grows down into the soil.
lessons.why: Roots take in water from the soil.

lessons.title: Explore changing matter
lessons.text: Water can be solid ice or liquid water. When ice gets warm enough, it melts into liquid water. When liquid water gets cold enough, it freezes into ice.
lessons.q: What happens when an ice cube melts?
lessons.hint: Think about what you see around an ice cube on a warm plate.
lessons.why: Melting changes solid ice into liquid water.

projects.title: Build a bridge for a toy.
projects.description: Use paper and blocks to help a small toy cross a gap. Work with a grown-up.
steps: Place two stacks of books a short distance apart on a table.
Try using a sheet of paper to make a bridge between them.
Fold the paper and try again. Does the bridge hold more weight?
Draw your bridge and tell a grown-up what you changed.

projects.title: Be a good listener.
projects.description: Take turns telling a story with a family member or trusted friend.
steps: Choose something that made you smile today.
Tell your partner about it while they listen.
Switch roles and listen to their story.
Tell your partner one thing you remember from their story.
